thread:
carlos: FYI customer reported AWS marketplace promo credits never landed on their org (org-8876). AWS order 01234-567890. They subscribed 3 days ago.

mia: thanks — can you drop the subscription ID + the customer's Redwood org id again? also which region was the marketplace purchase in?

carlos: Subscription ID: SUB-98765. Org: org-8876. Region: us-east-1. Customer says the marketplace invoice shows promo applied on AWS side.

taylor: tagging billing to triage @taylor :eyes:

aws-marketplace-bot: New subscription event received: SUB-98765 (order 01234-567890)

mia: I tried a lookup on the internal sync: run this from support tools and paste output:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/internal/billing/marketplace/orders/01234-567890
```

carlos: pasted output from customer CLI — got a 404 from our endpoint.

mia: ok can you paste the relevant logs from billing-service (last 24h) — looking for reconcileCredits or marketplace webhook errors

carlos: log snippet from billing-service: 
```
2026-03-16T14:22:11Z ERROR billing-service reconcileCredits order=01234-567890 status=404 reason="MarketplaceOrder not found in catalog" trace=aa11bb
2026-03-16T14:22:12Z WARN billing-sync webhook retry=1 event=subscription.created order=01234-567890
```

mia: looks like our webhook consumer couldn't find the marketplace SKU mapping. could be mismatch between AWS order id and the SKU we expect.

katie: can you confirm whether this customer used a partner promo (accelerator) or an AWS Marketplace promo? sometimes partner promos require a separate tag on the subscription.

carlos: customer says it was an AWS Marketplace promotional credit (promo code from AWS console).

taylor: i'm going to try a manual reconcile: if we confirm the amount from AWS invoice we can apply the credit on our side and then request AWS to reconcile their billing. please share invoice PDF or amount.

carlos: invoice PDF uploaded to the ticket — promo shows $5k credit on AWS invoice; subscription net charge $0.

mia: steps i'm doing now: 1) check our orders table for order 01234-567890 2) check sku_mapping table for marketplace sku 9876-aws-promocode 3) if missing, create temporary mapping and run reconcile job.

mia: quick query result: orders table has a record but marketplace_sku is NULL. SKU mapping missing -> webhook dropped with 404.

taylor: plan: apply a one-time manual credit of $5,000 to org-8876 to match AWS invoice, mark ticket as billing-adjusted, then open partner reconciliation with AWS (CC customer).

carlos: pls proceed — customer is watching, they need this week for month-end reporting.

katie: noted. @taylor do we need legal signoff for partner promos?

taylor: not for manual adjustments < $10k — going ahead. I'll also attach reconciliation request to AWS Partner Support: case REF-RED-20260316.

aws-marketplace-bot: Partner reconciliation request submitted: REF-RED-20260316

taylor: credits applied manually to org-8876: $5,000. Created internal note and set ticket to "pending partner reconciliation". Asked AWS to confirm.

carlos: customer confirmed they see the credit applied in their Redwood billing portal now. :thumbsup:

mia: leaving a short postmortem in the ticket: root cause missing SKU mapping for that marketplace promo flow, adding a guard in webhook consumer to route unknown SKUs to a holding queue instead of 404-drop.

taylor: will follow up with product on adding a signal to the onboarding flow to capture partner promo SKUs.

carlos: thanks team — closing out once AWS confirms reconciliation.

katie: nice fast response everyone. :party:
